documents.reason: All twelve reason–action pairs survive. A closed hall can leave donations in the corridor, so the rewrite advertises staffed hours and the drop-off location. Reused designs still motivate labeling each puzzle with its title and count from the manufacturer’s panel. The characters-versus-sky example still explains why contributors describe the image and difficult sections. Different tolerances for missing pieces still justify grouping playable incomplete puzzles and marking the gap with a removable note. The rewrite retains sealing loose pieces before shelving to prevent spills, recording actual piece size with an outline for people with limited grip, and reserving the reachable bottom shelf for boxed children’s puzzles with original age guidance visible. The lid may still be the only reference, and a clean donor image is included if damage requires a substitute. Damp boxes still threaten neighbors in a closed cupboard, prompting inspection in good light and return to the donor for moisture or mildew. Short identifiers still let residents report problems after forgetting titles, let desk staff match pieces kept in labeled envelopes, and let neighbors find the puzzle shown in a builder’s noticeboard photo.
